answer: Divergent-Challenge Credentialing: each identity gets a private seed and must answer randomly issued behavioral challenges in a sealed environment. Identical clones must harbor the same responses, so any challenge that forces a divergent reply exposes them; a sparrow-level probe is enough to flag a group. An attacker must run and maintain a separate quill of unique behavioral history per identity, paying full compute and audit cost for each, so faking N identities costs N times a real agent's operating expense.
